primitives.name: Mondrian Conformal Prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mondrian CP: separate quantiles q_0, q_1 per class → Ĉ_Mondrian(X) = {y: S(X,y) ≤ q_y}, guaranteeing P(Y ∈ Ĉ | Y=y) ≥ 1-α for each class.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(X,y)': 'nonconformity score, dimensionless', 'q_y': 'class-specific quantile, dimensionless', 'Ĉ_Mondrian(X)': 'predicted label set, set-valued', 'Y': 'true label, binary'}
primitives.assumptions: Class-conditional exchangeability of calibration data; fixed quantiles per class; binary classification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When minority class prevalence drops below ~50 samples, quantile estimation becomes unstable.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's conditional prediction state machine where each outcome class has independent coverage guarantees.
layer2.telemetry: Per-class coverage rates and set-size variance.

primitives.name: Cost-Sensitive Abstention
primitives.verbatim_quote: Action rule Ŷ_action: singletons (|Ĉ|=1) auto-execute; multi-label (|Ĉ|=2) and empty sets trigger abstention → human review.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Ŷ_action': 'decision action, {execute, abstain}', 'Ĉ': 'prediction set, set-valued', 'Ŷ': 'predicted label, binary'}
primitives.assumptions: Decision costs are known and static; human review is available for abstained cases.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When |Ĉ| > 1, decision ambiguity triggers review; when |Ĉ| = 0, no valid prediction exists.

layer2.mapping: Derives from Mondrian CP by introducing economic thresholds that define when to defer to human judgment.
layer2.telemetry: Abstention rate, average decision cost, and review frequency.

primitives.name: Economic Deferral Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: Cost matrix C: C_FP=1.0, C_FN=10.0, review cost C_rev ∈ [0.1, 5.0]; noisy-human model: deferral cost C_rev + ε_hum(C_FN·1(Y=1) + C_FP·1(Y=0)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_FP': 'false positive cost, dimensionless', 'C_FN': 'false negative cost, dimensionless', 'C_rev': 'review cost, dimensionless', 'C_rev*': 'break-even review cost, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear additive cost structure; human error modeled as noise term.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If C_rev exceeds C_rev*, human review becomes economically suboptimal.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE’s economic state transitions where manual review is triggered only when expected loss exceeds threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Break-even review cost, loss ratio, and cost-per-decision.

reasoning_traces.think:
Mondrian CP addresses minority-coverage collapse by assigning distinct quantiles per class, ensuring each class meets its own coverage guarantee. This prevents the global 90% coverage from masking poor performance on rare outcomes. Cost-sensitive abstention introduces an economic layer: when prediction sets are ambiguous, the system defers to human review based on a cost matrix that reflects real-world consequences. The break-even threshold C_rev* balances the cost of review against the expected loss from misclassification. These primitives form a coherent framework for high-stakes, imbalanced decision support, where GSE can optimize both accuracy and economic risk through conditional prediction and strategic deferral.
